items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: The claims connect: frontier, then safety, then the gap between the two Atlas models, then the Open-70B detail, and they match their tables row by row. One sentence is wrong on the page's own figures. Claim latency calls troubleshooting 'the slowest task', but in the appendix research-needed questions is slower for every model at p95 (Atlas-L 4.86 s vs 4.68 s, Atlas-M 2.84 s vs 2.73 s, Brisk-S 1.22 s vs 1.17 s, Open-70B 2.16 s vs 2.08 s). items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: Atlas-M's weak axis, overall quality against Atlas-L, is plain to see, and the 0% traffic share of speculation bait is flagged. But the decision block, the 'What you could change' table and the frontier caption all say Open-70B is never the best buy, at every price. That holds only on point estimates. Open-70B's pooled lead over Brisk-S is +0.79, with an unpaired interval of -0.19 to +1.77 (price.brisk-s.open-70b.overall.gain_interval_unpaired). So the price per point from Brisk-S to Open-70B runs from $3.11 upward with no top end, which reaches below the $4.15 edge of the Brisk-S/Atlas-M band.

items.name: Sound elision

Open-70B's per-task strength in persona small talk is shown in claim open70b and followed up in the next steps.

items.name: Confounds handled

The high confidence over open caveats is acceptable here, because the page makes no call and each clause says which direction the caveat would push.
